MAQm- He’s very knowledgeable, he knows lot about this course, so he tries to teach his students a lot(90 mins class e almost puratai porabe), sometimes it’s gonna be hard to keep attention, but try to understand and note down everything he teaches in the class, doing assignments by yourself and attending classes would be enough for mid and final preparation, project is very important because sir himself check the project, doing good in the project will increase your possibilities to get a good grade
STI- Maam teaches really well, her classes are enough to understand all the concepts. Exam e questions easy e thake, but u have to be quick. She provides also very detailed slides
Kmm- Sir is super cool. He covers all the basics concepts and gives questions from slides and class practice problems. There will be a short project which carries 10/15% marks

comments.text:
1. MAT481, MAT483, MAT485/MAT370
2. Comes down to the course requirements for Masters/PhD programs. Masters programs in Applied Mathematics tend to require almost all of those courses (minus MAT482) afaik. For AI/ML, MAT481 is the closest in terms of relevance. MAT485 would've been closer if it was a course on general optimization, rather than just linear optimization. MAT370 is great if you want to dabble to the more theory-heavy aspects of AI, because the course would equip you with a stronger understanding of mathematics. MAT483 if you're into Robotics; it can also be useful in other areas of AI, but not a necessity.
3. MAT483. You need to have a strong grasp of linear algebra.
4. MAT481. Course is a bit formulaic. You can just practice methods to get A, even without comprehending what's going on.
5. Not much of a choice here. These courses are normally assigned the same faculties, but in case not, MLA (MAT481), MTH (MAT483), HAr (MAT485).
6. Lol, barely a crumb in Bangladesh. These courses are mere stepping stones for your Masters or research, not proof of competence in the wild.
7. Yes, but you should actually go to the admissions pages of your desired university programs, and check the requirements.
8. For me, I wouldn't say so, but that's because I didn't come away from these courses as a more enlightened person. Maybe, it will be different in your case, if you thoroughly study these topics outside of the classroom, because the books contain more in-depth and elaborate contents than any faculty can teach you (understandably so; they don't have all the time in the world). That being said, all that effort may pay off once I start applying for Masters programs.
